item.title: Daily Brief — Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description:
The Milwaukee Brewers took Game 1 of the World Series 3-2 over the Tampa Bay Rays at American Family Field, grabbing an early edge in the best-of-seven. The decisive moment came in the top of the ninth, with Tampa Bay threatening to tie before the rally was snuffed out.

  • Jonny DeLuca [0-4 | RC 45] struck out swinging to end the top of the 9th with the tying run stranded, sealing Milwaukee's 3-2 win in Game 1. (TB)
  • Jacob Misiorowski [5 IP, 1 ER, 3 K | 1.81 ERA, PAR 78] turned in the day's top pitching line for the Brewers over 5 innings. (MIL)
  • Nick Martinez [5 IP, 2 ER, 5 K | 3.10 ERA, PAR 49] matched him with a strong 5-inning start in the loss for Tampa Bay. (TB)
  • Jonathan Aranda [3-3, 1 BB | RC 90] led all hitters with a perfect 3-for-3 day for the Rays. (TB)
  • William Contreras [2-3, 1 BB | RC 80] chipped in a two-hit game for Milwaukee. (MIL)

item.title: Daily Brief — Monday, October 19, 2026
item.description:
The Tampa Bay Rays won the American League pennant, closing out the Cleveland Guardians in six games with a 7-3 victory at Tropicana Field. The decisive blow came early, as Tampa Bay built its lead in the second inning and never looked back.

  • Richie Palacios [2-4 | RC 43] opened the scoring with a two-run double in the bottom of the 2nd, staking the Rays to a 2-0 lead on the way to a 7-3 win that clinched the ALCS 4-2. (TB)
  • Freddy Peralta [5.1 IP, 1 ER, 3 K | 4.42 ERA, PAR 31] anchored the clincher with 5.1 innings of one-run ball. (TB)
  • Junior Caminero [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 116] homered and reached base three times to pace the Tampa Bay offense. (TB)
  • Yandy Díaz [1-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 98] added a two-run shot in the win. (TB)
  • Nathaniel Lowe [2-3, 1 BB | RC 54] had the lone standout night for Cleveland with a 2-for-3 effort. (CLE)

item.title: Daily Brief — Sunday, October 18, 2026
item.description:
The Tampa Bay Rays moved within one win of the pennant, taking Game 5 of the ALCS 3-1 at Progressive Field to push Cleveland to the brink of elimination. The Guardians now face elimination in Game 6.

  • Chase DeLauter [1-3, 1 BB | RC 82] drew a bottom-9th walk to bring the tying run to the plate, but the rally stalled as Tampa Bay closed out the 3-1 win and a 3-2 series lead. (CLE)
  • Drew Rasmussen [7 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 2.67 ERA, PAR 62] was dominant for the Rays, carrying the game with seven strong innings of one-run ball. (TB)
  • Liam Hicks [2-3, 1 BB | RC 76] paced the Tampa Bay offense at the plate. (TB)
  • Yandy Díaz [3-5 | RC 98] added a three-hit day in the Rays' win. (TB)
  • Chandler Simpson [2-3 | RC 68] chipped in a multi-hit effort at the top of the order. (TB)
  • Steven Kwan [2-4 | RC 72] led the Cleveland offense in the losing effort. (CLE)

item.title: Daily Brief — Saturday, October 17, 2026
item.description:
The Rays evened the ALCS at two games apiece with a 7-3 win in Cleveland, flipping a game they'd fallen to 34% win probability in and setting up a pivotal Game 5 with the series knotted.

  • Junior Caminero [1-5 | RC 116]'s sixth-inning double to left scored Jonathan Aranda [3-4, 1 BB | RC 90] to put Tampa Bay ahead 2-1 for good in the Rays' 7-3 win at Progressive Field. (TB)
  • Nick Martinez [5.1 IP, 1 ER, 3 K | 3.10 ERA, PAR 49] turned in the night's top start, working into the sixth and holding Cleveland to one earned run. (TB)
  • Foster Griffin [3.2 IP, 1 ER, 5 K | 3.61 ERA, PAR 42] was sharp in a losing effort, striking out five over 3.2 innings. (CLE)
  • Travis Bazzana [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 61] led all hitters with a home run among his two hits for Cleveland. (CLE)
  • Jonathan Aranda and Richie Palacios [3-4 | RC 43] each went 3-for-4 at the top of the Rays' attack, with Yandy Díaz [2-5, 1 HR | RC 98] adding a homer. (TB)

item.title: Daily Brief — Thursday, October 15, 2026
item.description:
The Milwaukee Brewers clinched the NL pennant, finishing off the Los Angeles Dodgers in a four-game sweep behind a comeback from a 4-0 deficit. In the ALCS, Cleveland took a 2-1 series lead over Tampa Bay with a one-run win at Progressive Field.

  • Chandler Simpson [1-3 | RC 68]'s go-ahead triple in the top of the 4th scored two and swung the game Tampa's way, but Cleveland still edged the Rays 3-2 to take a 2-1 ALCS lead. (TB)
  • Will Smith [1-4 | RC 36]'s 8th-inning double, extended to a triple on a Sal Frelick [0-3, 1 BB | RC 32] error, pulled the Dodgers within one — but Milwaukee held on 6-4 to sweep the NLCS and reach the World Series. (LAD)
  • Gavin Williams [5 IP, 2 ER, 9 K | 3.76 ERA, PAR 49] was dominant for Cleveland, striking out nine over five innings. (CLE)
  • David Hamilton [2-4, 1 HR | RC 36] led the Brewers' offense with a two-hit night including a home run. (MIL)
  • José Ramírez [2-3, 1 BB | RC 56] went 2-for-3 and Petey Halpin [1-3, 1 HR | RC 16] homered in the Guardians' win. (CLE)
  • Garrett Mitchell [1-4, 1 HR | RC 68] and Shohei Ohtani [1-4, 1 HR] also went deep in the NLCS clincher. (MIL)

item.description:

  • Jake Bauers [1-4, 1 HR | RC 90] flipped the game in the top of the 7th with a two-run homer that scored Christian Yelich [0-1 | RC 53], pushing Milwaukee ahead 3-2 en route to a 6-2 win. (MIL)

item.description:

  • Freddy Peralta [6 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 4.42 ERA, PAR 31] was dominant for the Rays, tossing six shutout innings with six strikeouts. (TB)

item.title: Daily Brief — Monday, October 12, 2026
item.description:
The Milwaukee Brewers took a commanding 2-0 lead in the NLCS with a win over the Dodgers, while the Guardians stole Game 1 of the ALCS from the Rays in Tampa after trailing late. Cleveland's comeback produced the day's biggest WPA swing.

  • Christian Yelich [2-5 | RC 53]'s two-run single in the bottom of the 3rd put Milwaukee ahead for good, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 7-4 to go up 2-0 in the NLCS. (MIL)
  • Chase DeLauter [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 82]'s go-ahead double in the top of the 8th capped Cleveland's rally from a 2-1 deficit, lifting the Guardians over the Rays 7-3 for a 1-0 ALCS lead. (CLE)
  • Drew Rasmussen [6 IP, 2 ER, 7 K | 2.67 ERA, PAR 62] was dominant in the loss, posting the day's top pitching line for Tampa Bay. (TB)

item.description:

item.title: Daily Brief — Saturday, October 10, 2026
item.description:

item.title: Daily Brief — Wednesday, October 7, 2026
item.description:
Three Division Series ended on October 7, with the Rays sweeping the Yankees, the Dodgers closing out the Braves, and the Brewers finishing off the Padres. The lone series still alive is in the AL Central, where the White Sox lead the Guardians 2-1 and Cleveland now faces elimination in Game 4.

  • Victor Mesa Jr. [1-4, 1 HR | RC 38]'s top-6th two-run homer put Tampa Bay ahead for good in a 4-3 win over the Yankees, completing a 3-0 sweep. (TB)
  • Andy Pages [2-3 | RC 82]'s top-7th two-run single broke open a 4-1 Dodgers win in Atlanta, clinching the NLDS 3-1. (LAD)
  • Fernando Tatis Jr. [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 105]'s bottom-3rd solo homer briefly tied it, but Milwaukee pulled away for a 3-1 win and a 3-1 series clincher over San Diego. (SD)
  • Jo Adell [2-4, 1 BB | RC 72]'s top-3rd three-run triple fueled Cleveland's 9-3 rout of the White Sox, the day's biggest comeback after the Guardians trailed 1-0; Chicago still leads the series 2-1. (CLE)
  • Tyler Mahle [6.1 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 3.99 ERA, PAR 33] was sharp in a losing effort for Atlanta. (ATL)
  • Foster Griffin [2.2 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 3.61 ERA, PAR 42] struck out seven in relief for Cleveland. (CLE)
